speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the breast mass you found, specifically its location, size, and whether it is painful?

speaker: Patient
text: 48-year-old woman. The patient noticed a mass in her left breast 4 weeks ago, which has rapidly increased in size. She denies any recent trauma or infections. No history of similar complaints in the past.

speaker: Doctor
text: Is the mass hard and fixed to the surrounding tissue, or is it soft and mobile? Also, have you noticed any skin changes like dimpling, redness, or nipple discharge?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Presence of a left breast mass. I also have Rapid increase in size of the mass, No skin or nipple changes, No pain associated with the mass.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the rapid growth over just four weeks without pain or skin changes, I need to rule out an inflammatory or phyllodes tumor versus a high-grade carcinoma. REQUEST TEST: Mammography and Ultrasound of the Left Breast.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Mammography: Smooth polylobulated mass in the left breast.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any personal or family history of breast cancer or genetic mutations like BRCA? Also, are you currently pregnant or breastfeeding?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical or surgical history. No family history of breast cancer. Social history: Non-smoker, moderate alcohol use. Elementary school teacher.

speaker: Doctor
text: The rapid growth and smooth, polylobulated appearance on mammography are highly suggestive of a phyllodes tumor rather than a typical carcinoma. I need to confirm the cellular composition and margins to rule out malignancy. REQUEST TEST: Core needle biopsy of the left breast mass.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Biopsy Microscopic Description: Image shows leaf-like structures with stromal cellular overgrowth.

speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy showing leaf-like structures with stromal cellular overgrowth is diagnostic. DIAGNOSIS READY: Phyllodes tumor
